page: Microsoft Azure D4_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is driven by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores utilizing 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512, VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight consistent single-threaded execution set against throughput limitations inherent to a 4-vCPU footprint. The instance scored 1897.28 in stress-ng single-core and 1653.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, placing it in the median performance bracket. Data handling benchmarks reflect average single-thread gzip compression at 28.57 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.42 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded scaling remains in the lower quartile, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 3526.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5868.76. Uncached memory operations register 29.82 GB/sec for 256MB block reads and 25.45 GB/sec for writes, sustaining static web serving throughput of 6.6 GB/sec and lightweight LLM prompt processing of 500.6 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models.

From an architectural standpoint, the D4_v5 delivers balanced resource allocation without the cost overhead associated with attached local NVMe drives or GPU silicon. Because local instance storage is absent, the machine requires network-attached storage for non-volatile requirements. This profile presents an efficient baseline for general-purpose computing tasks that demand steady single-core CPU speeds rather than dense parallel compute. Common suitable workloads include web servers, microservice container hosting, application gateways, small database backends, and standard continuous integration jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D4_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading and 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 48 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptographic extensions, and AVX-512 support, but provides no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the D4_v5 exhibits dependable single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 1653.0 and steady static web throughput of 6.6 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations and uncached memory bandwidth reflect the limitations of its four-vCPU scale, scoring 3526.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 3.98 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. This profile makes the instance cost-efficient for standard enterprise tasks, including static web serving, containerized microservices, light data parsing, and general-purpose business application backends relying on external storage.
